decisions.quote:
First, experiments JA11 and JA12 constituted exact replications of the procedures reported in Alfei et al. (2015, 
experiment 5) and Ferrer Monti et al. (2017, experiment 2).
decisions.reason: The prior adjudication file is absent and the prior state file records only an unresolved CLI timeout. The paper explicitly conducts direct/exact replications (experiments JA09, JA10, JA11, JA12, and NS09) and procedural variations (experiments NS10, NS12-NS14, NS18, NS21, including post-extinction MDZ in NS14) of Ferrer Monti et al. (2017, Experiment 2, 10.1101/lm.045385.117), testing whether systemic post-reactivation midazolam (3 mg/kg after a 2-min contextual fear reactivation session) induces amnesia. The only shipped row for this work is input_row_index 2487, which is Alfei et al. (2015, 10.1101/lm.038513.115). Although both original studies used the same 2-min reactivation and 3 mg/kg MDZ protocol in the Córdoba laboratory, Table 1 and Results Section 3.2 establish that they are independent published papers reporting distinct original experiments with different samples and effect sizes (Alfei et al., 2015, Exp. 5, N=18, d=1.80 vs. Ferrer Monti et al., 2017, Exp. 2, N=12, d=3.88), so report equivalence does not apply.

decisions.quote:
Second, 
MDZ  was  administered  after  extinction,  in  line  with  prior  publications  showing  that  MDZ  can  interfere  with 
extinction consolidation (Alfei et al., 2015; Bustos et al., 2009; Ferrer Monti et al., 2017; Franzen, Giachero, & 
Bertoglio, 2019). We adopted training parameters from Alfei et al. (2015) and Ferrer Monti et al. (2017) and 
administered MDZ (or SAL) after a 30-min re-exposure session, but did not replicate their results, suggesting 
that MDZ did not affect extinction consolidation.
decisions.reason: The prior adjudication file is absent and the prior state file records only an unresolved CLI timeout. Franzen et al. (2019, 10.1016/j.neuroscience.2019.03.035) is not empirically retested in this paper. It is included in Table 1's literature compilation of MDZ studies published up to April 2019 and cited as background in the Discussion regarding extinction consolidation and between-session control freezing decreases. As the Discussion explicitly states, the extinction consolidation experiment (NS14) adopted training parameters from and tested Alfei et al. (2015, shipped row 2487) and Ferrer Monti et al. (2017, target_index 10), and all experiments in the current paper used male rats (Section 2.2) rather than testing Franzen et al.'s (2019) estrous-cycle findings in female rats.

decisions.reason: The prior adjudication file is absent and the prior state file records only an unresolved CLI timeout. Contrary to Luna triage, Gazarini et al. (2015, 10.1093/ijnp/pyu026) is cited only in a five-paper background citation alongside Bustos et al. (2010), Espejo et al. (2016, 2017), and Ortiz et al. (2015) as prior motivation for using pre-reactivation D-cycloserine (DCS) to promote destabilization of resistant fear memories. Gazarini et al. (2015) investigated a PTSD-like memory generated through enhanced noradrenergic activity (and is not even part of the MDZ/PROP studies in Tables 1-2). As Section 2.9.4 and Section 2.9.6 explain, experiment NS12 was a procedural variation on Alfei et al. (2015, shipped row 2487) and Ferrer Monti et al. (2017, target_index 10) adding pre-reactivation DCS before post-reactivation MDZ, and experiment NS20 applied pre-reactivation DCS + post-reactivation MDZ to the authors' own 3-day training protocol from NS17; neither experiment retests Gazarini et al. (2015).
